tasks.title: Language layer as data: extension map and four node-type tables

details.goal: Language support as a table lookup, with provenance established by probing the real grammars.
details.contract: types.ts exports type LangId (the 12 MVP ids: python, typescript, tsx, javascript, go, java, rust, c, cpp, csharp, php, ruby), interface LangSpec { id, extensions: string[], grammarWasm: string, classTypes: string[], functionTypes: string[], importTypes: string[], callTypes: string[], inheritanceTypes: string[], testFileRegex?: RegExp }, and the resolved row type. registry.ts exports EXTENSION_MAP (ext to LangId, deterministic order, includes .py .ts .tsx .js .jsx .mjs .cjs .go .java .rs .c .h .cpp .cc .hpp .cs .php .rb), LANGS (LangId to LangSpec), detectLanguage(path): LangId | null, and specFor(id). The four node-type lists are the node-versus-edge decision expressed as data: classTypes produce class nodes, functionTypes produce function nodes, importTypes and callTypes produce edges, inheritanceTypes name the grammar node carrying a superclass or interface clause. Provenance is established by runtime probe, not by reading vendored node-types: TASK-013 parses one snippet per language and this task's test asserts every list matches at least one real node in the loaded grammar. Do not claim the lists were validated against a vendored node-types file.
steps: Write types.ts with LangId, LangSpec including inheritanceTypes, and the row type
Write registry.ts with EXTENSION_MAP for the 12 languages
Fill the four node-type lists plus inheritanceTypes per language
Implement detectLanguage and specFor
Write tests/lang.test.ts asserting function, call and inheritance lists are non-empty and that .h maps to c while .cpp maps to cpp
Add a probe assertion that each declared node type exists in the loaded grammar for that language
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/lang.test.ts. Done when all 12 languages pass the type-list and probe assertions, every extension resolves, and .h maps to c.

tasks.title: WASM parser pool with a bounded per-language LRU

details.goal: One parser entry point that loads a grammar on demand, bounds memory, and returns a tree plus any parse-error ranges.
details.contract: parse.ts exports initParsers(): Promise<void> (initialises the web-tree-sitter runtime once per process), parseFile(path, source, lang): Promise<{tree, errorRanges: string[]}> and disposeLang(lang). Grammars load from tree-sitter-wasms in node_modules by the grammarWasm name in the LangSpec; a missing grammar resolves to an error with reason grammar_unavailable, never a throw out of parseFile. Parser instances are cached in an LRU of max 6 languages keyed by LangId, each with a reset() before reuse. errorRanges is computed by walking the tree for ERROR and MISSING nodes and formatting as comma-separated 1-based line ranges with a cap of 20 ranges plus a count suffix. No file may be parsed twice concurrently in this module. Package versions are @modelcontextprotocol/sdk independent: web-tree-sitter 0.27.2, tree-sitter-wasms 0.1.13 as installed by TASK-001.
steps: Write initParsers using web-tree-sitter Parser.init()
Implement the language LRU with reset-before-reuse
Implement parseFile mapping LangSpec.grammarWasm to the wasm file and returning errorRanges
Handle an unavailable grammar as a structured result rather than an exception
Write tests/parse.test.ts parsing one Python and one TypeScript snippet and asserting errorRanges is empty
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/parse.test.ts. Done when both snippets parse with zero error ranges, and a request for a fabricated grammar returns reason grammar_unavailable without throwing.

tasks.title: Repository discovery with exclusions and coverage reasons

details.goal: Walk a repository deterministically and record both what is indexed and what is skipped, with a reason.
details.contract: discover.ts exports discover(repoRoot, {ignorePatterns?}): Promise<{files: Array<{path, lang, size, sha256}>, notIndexed: Array<{path, reason, language?}>, skipped: number}>. Rules: always exclude .git, node_modules, .codegraph, dist, vendor; honour repoRoot/.gitignore and repoRoot/.codegraphignore with simple glob matching; skip files larger than 512 MiB with reason size_cap; skip binary files (NUL byte in the first 8192 bytes) with reason binary; record a file whose extension is unknown as reason unsupported_ext; compute sha256 for every accepted file. Paths are repo-relative with forward slashes and no leading dot-slash. Deterministic ordering by path so two runs produce identical output.
steps: Implement the recursive walk with the always-exclude list
Add .gitignore and .codegraphignore parsing with glob matching
Add the binary, size and unsupported-extension classifications with reasons
Compute sha256 for accepted files and sort by path
Write tests/discover.test.ts over a temp tree containing one .ts file, one binary, one unknown extension and one ignored path
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/discover.test.ts. Done when the fixture yields exactly one indexed file and three notIndexed entries with reasons ignored, binary and unsupported_ext, in deterministic order.

tasks.title: Generic table-driven extractor for nodes, containment and raw edges

details.goal: One cursor walk driven by the node-type tables that produces nodes, calls, imports, inheritance and reference sites.
details.contract: extract.ts exports extractFile(tree, spec, relPath): {nodes, rawEdges, unresolved}. Node kinds: file, module, class, function, method, test, endpoint; each node carries name, qn as relPath::Scope.name, startLine, endLine, signature, isTest, props. Walk rules: classTypes emit a class node and push onto the scope stack; functionTypes inside a class emit method, outside emit function; callTypes emit kind calls; importTypes emit kind imports; inheritanceTypes emit kind inherits when the clause names a class and implements when it names an interface, tier extracted_candidate. VALUE-POSITION REFERENCE SITES ARE PRODUCED HERE: an identifier appearing as a call argument, an assignment right-hand side, an object/array literal element, a decorator argument or a return expression emits a rawEdge kind references with the identifier text as target and tier extracted_candidate; this is what the bind pass resolves so the references group in trace is not permanently empty. Unnameable sites inside calls or imports go to unresolved with evidence_kind dynamic. contains edges run from the enclosing file or class to every declared node. The file node is always first. No language-specific branches beyond a documented exception table of at most 3 entries.
steps: Write the scope stack and the file and module node emission
Implement classTypes and functionTypes with the method versus function distinction
Implement callTypes and importTypes collecting unresolved sites in the same pass
Implement inheritanceTypes producing inherits and implements
Implement value-position references rawEdges for the six site kinds listed in the contract
Write tests/extract.test.ts over a Python fixture asserting every kind, the qn form, one inherits edge and at least one references site
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/extract.test.ts. Done when the fixture yields file, class, method and function nodes with the path::Class.method qn form, at least one inherits rawEdge, at least one references rawEdge, one contains edge per declaration, and no unresolved entry.

tasks.title: Binding pass: resolve raw edges by same-file, import and inheritance evidence

details.goal: Bind calls, imports, inheritance and reference sites into real edges, dropping ambiguous references.
details.contract: resolve.ts exports bind(units: FileUnit[], index: SymbolIndex): {edges, unresolved}. Binding order for a call or import target: exact qn in the same file, then a name visible through that file's imports, then a unique name in the whole index, then a superclass method when the receiver's class inherits it, otherwise unresolved with evidence_kind receiver_type_unknown, ambiguous or dynamic. Tiers: extracted for same-file and import evidence, inferred for unique-name and inheritance evidence. THIS PASS ALSO FINALISES THE NON-CALL EDGES: resolved inherits and implements rawEdges become real edges at tier extracted; references rawEdges from the extractor become real edges at tier inferred when exactly one node matches and are DROPPED silently when zero or several match, because a spurious reference is worse than a missing one. tested_by is not produced here; the persist task derives it. Never emit an edge whose target id does not exist.
steps: Define SymbolIndex construction from units including per-file import tables
Implement the four-step binding order with tiers
Emit resolved inherits and implements at tier extracted
Resolve references at tier inferred and drop ambiguous or unmatched ones
Route every call and import failure to unresolved with the matching evidence_kind
Write tests/resolve.test.ts covering the five binding cases plus inherits and references
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/resolve.test.ts. Done when the five call-binding cases behave as specified, one resolved inherits edge and one resolved references edge exist, an ambiguous reference is dropped rather than emitted, and no edge targets a missing node.

tasks.title: Persist a generation: metrics, FTS delta, tombstones

details.goal: Write one unit set into the stage and derive metrics, tested_by with an explicit direction decision, FTS and tombstones.
details.contract:
persist.ts exports persistUnit(tx, unit, resolved) writing nodes, edges, unresolved and not_indexed for one file after deleting that file's previous rows by file_id; and finalizeGeneration(tx, {generationId, baseCommit, mode}) returning {nodes, edges, tombstones} which recomputes node_metrics for touched nodes plus their two-hop neighbourhood, updates node_fts_state and node_fts by rowid delta, appends a tombstone per disappeared qn, and inserts the generation row plus meta.generation.
TESTED_BY IS DERIVED HERE, and its direction is a decision that must be recorded in the code: for every node with is_test = 1, follow its outgoing calls edges into non-test nodes and emit tested_by with SOURCE = the test node and TARGET = the tested symbol, tier inferred. That inverts the CRG direction documented in GRAPH-MODEL.md section 4 (there, function to test) and is deliberate: it makes tested_by appear in the queried symbol's inbound group, which is what TOOLS-SPEC.md section 3 renders. Set tested_depth = 1 for those targets, 2 for nodes one further call hop away, NULL otherwise, so summary test_gaps is a column read. FTS delta falls back to a full rebuild above 35 percent of node rows. No function here opens a connection.
steps: Implement persistUnit with file-scoped delete then insert
Implement degree and tested_depth recomputation for the touched neighbourhood
Derive tested_by as test to symbol at tier inferred, with the direction comment
Implement the FTS delta with the 35 percent rebuild threshold
Append tombstones and insert the generation row
Write tests/persist.test.ts asserting a re-persist leaves one tombstone and a tested function has tested_depth 1
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/persist.test.ts. Done when a re-persist deletes the removed symbol, records exactly one tombstone, and a function called by a test node has a tested_by edge whose source is the test node and tested_depth 1.

tasks.title: Index worker entry: lock, incremental routing, publish, exit codes

details.goal: A standalone process that owns the writer and reports one machine-readable result, working with or without git.
details.contract: worker.ts exports runWorker(opts: {repoRoot, dataDir, force, mode}): Promise<number> returning 0 published, 2 nothing to do, 75 lock held, 1 failure. Sequence: acquireLock (index_locked returns 75), ensure data dir and .codegraph/.gitignore containing a single star, migrate, discover, compute changed files by comparing sha256 against the file table and, when repoRoot is a git repository, additionally using #shared/domain/diff changedSince — a non-git directory must degrade to hash-only comparison and still return 0, never 1. If nothing changed and not force return 2. withStage: persist each changed unit, bind edges, finalizeGeneration, seal, publish. On any throw: discard the stage, bump meta.consecutive_failures, set meta.indexer_state to failed, return 1. On success set indexer_state to idle. stdout must stay empty; all reporting is on stderr or the exit code. Invoked by bin/codegraph.ts worker mode and by the watcher; tools must never import it.
steps: Implement option parsing and the lock acquisition with the 75 exit code
Implement data dir setup including the single-star .gitignore
Implement the incremental changed-file computation with the non-git fallback
Implement the withStage orchestration calling persistUnit and finalizeGeneration
Implement success and failure metadata writes and exit codes
Write tests/worker.test.ts running runWorker on a non-git temp repo twice, expecting 0 then 2
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/worker.test.ts. Done when the first run on a non-git directory returns 0 with one generation row, the second returns 2, and stdout captured during both runs is empty.

tasks.title: Phase 1 closing gate: parser parity and full-corpus index

details.goal: Prove the indexer meets every acceptance criterion against oracles that exist and are consistent with the MVP language set.
details.contract: parser-parity.test.ts indexes code-review-graph/ read-only into a temp data dir and asserts only oracles that exist and that the 12-language set can actually produce: (a) totals within 5 percent of 13 955 nodes and 130 044 edges recorded in TOOL-OUTPUTS.md; (b) by-kind within 5 percent for four CRG kinds, with one stated mapping rule — CRG Function is compared against our function UNION method, because CRG has no separate Method kind; the other three are File 530, Class 877, Test 6 351; (c) per-language FILE counts within 5 percent restricted to the 12 supported languages (python 408, typescript 28, java 4, c 4, cpp 3, rust 3, go 2), and an explicit assertion that yaml, bash and r files appear in not_indexed with reason unsupported_ext — they are outside the MVP language set, so asserting counts for them would be asserting zero; (d) at most 1 percent of files may contain any ERROR node; (e) p50 parse at most 4 ms per file and p95 at most 25 ms over at least 200 files; (f) peak RSS at most 1 GB. index-integration.test.ts runs runWorker on the same corpus and asserts one generation row, non-zero unresolved rows, no not_indexed entry with reason unsupported_ext for a supported language, a second run returning 2, and the corpus unmodified measured by git -C code-review-graph status --porcelain being empty (the root repository ignores that directory, so a root git status proves nothing).
steps: Write tests/parser-parity.test.ts with the totals, mapped by-kind, restricted per-language file, unsupported_ext, ERROR, timing and RSS assertions
Write tests/index-integration.test.ts with the generation, unresolved, idempotence and corpus-clean assertions
Run both against code-review-graph/ and record the measured numbers
Confirm the corpus is unmodified using git -C code-review-graph status --porcelain
details.verify: cd app and run: $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/parser-parity.test.ts tests/index-integration.test.ts. Done when all assertions pass, RSS stayed under 1 GB, and the measured timing plus the mapped by-kind counts are recorded in the progress log.
